newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index inches up on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index inches up on foreign demand.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index inched up 6.81 points to close at 3472.59 boosted by strong demand from foreign investors on select key shares.
Turnover went up to 88.010 million shillings on 1,316,168 shares due to heavy activity on the special boards.
Foreigners bought 233,000 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 93 and 106, and 60,000 shares of East Africa Portland Cement at 36 from 33.

Brokers said there was pressure on the financials to trade at lower prices as speculators who had bought shares in anticipation of a bonus issue accompanying the year-end results released by Barclays Bank and Standard Chartered Bank on Friday offloaded their shares.
Investment analysts had predicted that the immediate beneficiaries would be key shares on other boards.
"I think what is happening is that investors are losing their herding instinct and beginning to make investment decisions on the individual merits of a company," a senior broker said.
Sasini Tea & Coffee gained 7.50 to close at 68, while Uchumi Supermarket closed at 41.50 from 41.
Barclays Bank eased to 110 from 111 while Standard Chartered Bank shed a shilling to close at 48 from 49. National Bank of Kenya edged to 15.75 from 15.50.
National carrier Kenya Airways closed at 8.80 from 8.70 while Nation Printers & Publishers eased to 109 from 110.
The East African Development Bank corporate bond traded 24 million shillings at 101.30 percent compared to 10 million shillings at 101.16 percent on March 3.
